metadata.scope: e_macedonia (12 non-867 baronies across k_hellas; excludes baronies where is_historical_at['867'] is true)
metadata.hierarchy_note: hierarchy reflects data/ck3_title_tree.json (save-derived de jure tree including x_script_* dynamic titles); downstream localisation/historicity mods should key on barony_key and join against their target landed_titles tree.

schema_notes.vanilla_ck3_name: Exact English localisation string from CK3 titles_l_english.yml.
schema_notes.modern_name: Clean modern/standard English display name of the audited settlement or holding.
schema_notes.modern_name_note: Optional administrative parent, alternate designation, or native-script qualifier; null if none.
schema_notes.hierarchy: De jure title hierarchy from data/ck3_title_tree.json (empire, kingdom, duchy, county, holding_type).
schema_notes.is_historical_at: Bookmark-keyed booleans {'867', '1066', '1178'}; all entries here have '867': false.
schema_notes.replacement_candidates: List of exactly 3 associated natural feature names and historical tribal/ethnonym names (>=1 tribe per barony) usable as localisation replacements.
schema_notes.name: Clean display name of the replacement candidate (Wikipedia disambiguation suffixes extracted to disambiguation_note).
schema_notes.disambiguation_note: Optional disambiguator extracted from parenthetical/comma qualifiers (e.g. 'Liao', 'Orkney', 'river'); null if none.
schema_notes.localisation_stem: Clean CK3-ready toponym stem stripped of redundant generic English feature suffixes/prefixes ('River', 'Mount', 'Lake', 'people', etc.) while preserving meaningful compounds.
schema_notes.attestation_basis: Historicity classification distinguishing genuinely pre-867/pre-literate entities from medieval post-867 ethnogeneses: attested_pre_867 | indigenous_pre_literate | attested_867_to_1066 | attested_1066_to_1178.
schema_notes.valid_for_bookmarks: Bookmark-keyed booleans {'867', '1066', '1178'} indicating whether the replacement candidate is historically non-anachronistic for that bookmark (true for both attested_pre_867 and indigenous_pre_literate; bookmark-gated for attested_867_to_1066 and attested_1066_to_1178).
schema_notes.candidates_with_multilingual_variants: Count of replacement candidates having more than 1 distinct language_code (ISO 639-3 / ISO 639-5 or documented proto-stage code) across language_variants.
schema_notes.language_variants_policy: Include core local/classical forms plus regionally scoped vernaculars and genuinely distinct exonyms; exclude out-of-region exonym padding and redundant eng copies (eng is retained only when no non-English variant exists). Uses ISO 639-3 / ISO 639-5 language_code values plus documented Wiktionary proto/stage codes (sla-pro, gem-pro, cel-pro, cel-bry, urj-fin-pro); reconstructed proto/ancient forms carry a leading '*'.
schema_notes.language_variants: List of cultural/historical name forms: {form, native_script, language, language_code, notes}. form is always clean Latin script (or romanization) suitable for CK3 localisation; native_script holds the native non-Latin script form or null when the language natively uses Latin script.
schema_notes.relationship: Prose description of the geographical, ecological, or historical relationship between the replacement entity and the audited barony.
schema_notes.etymology_notes: Linguistic etymology, onomastic origin, or geographic/ethnographic characterization of the replacement entity (incorporating attested onomastic notes from language variants where documented).

replacement_candidates.name: Achaeans
replacement_candidates.relationship: Ancient Greek tribe inhabiting Achaea in the northern Peloponnese.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Greek Akhaioi; one of the four major Hellenic tribes of classical antiquity.

replacement_candidates.name: Selinountas
replacement_candidates.relationship: River of Achaea flowing into the Gulf of Corinth near Aigio (Vostitsa).
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: From Ancient Greek selinon ('wild celery').

replacement_candidates.name: Panachaiko
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain massif overlooking northern Achaea and the Gulf of Corinth.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Greek Panakhaikon ('of all the Achaeans').

replacement_candidates.name: Dorians
replacement_candidates.relationship: Major ancient Greek tribe that settled across the Peloponnese.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Greek Dorieis, traditionally linked to Doris in central Greece.

replacement_candidates.name: Pineios
replacement_candidates.relationship: Main river of Elis flowing past Andravida into the Ionian Sea.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: c. 450 BCE (classical Greek sources on Elis, Strabo/Pausanias)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Classical Greek Peneios, shared with the Thessalian river.

replacement_candidates.name: Mount Erymanthos
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain massif on the border of Achaea and Elis.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Pre-Greek Aegean oronym attested since Homer.

replacement_candidates.name: Ezeritai
replacement_candidates.relationship: Early medieval Slavic tribe that settled in the Peloponnese.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: c. 950 CE (Constantine VII Porphyrogenitus, De Administrando Imperio 50)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: From South Slavic *jezero ('lake'), 'lake-dwellers'.

replacement_candidates.name: Vouraikos
replacement_candidates.relationship: River rising near Kalavryta and flowing through a deep gorge to the Gulf of Corinth.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Named after the ancient Achaean city of Boura.

replacement_candidates.name: Aroania
replacement_candidates.relationship: High mountain massif (Mount Chelmos) rising directly above Kalavryta.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Classical Greek Aroania; medieval Slavic name Chelmos from *chlŭmŭ ('hill/summit').

replacement_candidates.name: Pelasgians
replacement_candidates.relationship: Pre-Hellenic Aegean people associated with Arcadia and the Peloponnese.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Greek ethnonym for pre-classical inhabitants of Greece.

replacement_candidates.name: Alfeios
replacement_candidates.relationship: Longest river of the Peloponnese, rising in the Tegea-Tripoli basin near Nikli.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Greek Alpheios, attested since Homer.

replacement_candidates.name: Mainalo
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain massif overlooking the Tegea-Nikli plain in central Arcadia.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: c. 450 BCE (classical Greek poetry and Pausanias 8.36)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Greek Mainalos / Mainalon.

replacement_candidates.name: Dryopes
replacement_candidates.relationship: Ancient Greek tribe that settled in Asine and Hermione in Argolis.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Greek ethnonym, traditionally associated with oak-woodland (*drys).

replacement_candidates.name: Inachos
replacement_candidates.relationship: Principal river of Argolis in the northeastern Peloponnese.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Pre-Greek hydronym personified as the first king of Argos.

replacement_candidates.name: Saronic Gulf
replacement_candidates.relationship: Gulf of the Aegean Sea bordering Troezen (Damala) and Corinthia.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Named after the legendary King Saron of Troezen.

replacement_candidates.name: Melingoi
replacement_candidates.relationship: Slavic tribe that settled on the slopes of Mount Taygetus in Laconia.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: c. 950 CE (Constantine VII Porphyrogenitus, De Administrando Imperio 50)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Byzantine Greek rendering of a South Slavic tribal name in the Taygetus.

replacement_candidates.name: Evrotas
replacement_candidates.relationship: Main river of Laconia flowing through the Spartan plain below Mistra.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Greek Eurotas, attested in classical Spartan and Attic sources.

replacement_candidates.name: Taygetus
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain range on whose eastern foothills Mistra was built.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Pre-Greek oronym attested since Homer.

replacement_candidates.name: Ionians
replacement_candidates.relationship: One of the four major ancient Greek tribes with early Peloponnesian presence.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Greek Iaones / Iones.

replacement_candidates.name: Lousios
replacement_candidates.relationship: River flowing through a deep gorge just north of Karytaina into the Alfeios.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: From Greek louo ('to wash/bathe'), after the mythical bathing of infant Zeus.

replacement_candidates.name: Mount Lykaion
replacement_candidates.relationship: Sacred Arcadian mountain southwest of Karytaina.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: c. 470 BCE (Pindar, Olympian Odes, and Pausanias)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: From Greek lykos ('wolf') or lyke ('light').

replacement_candidates.name: Caucones
replacement_candidates.relationship: Ancient tribe of Triphylia and western Messenia near Kyparissia.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Pre-classical Aegean/Peloponnesian tribal name attested in the Odyssey and Herodotus.

replacement_candidates.name: Neda
replacement_candidates.relationship: River forming the border between Messenia and Elis north of Kyparissia.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: c. 170 CE (Pausanias, Description of Greece 4.20.1 and 8.41)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Named after the nymph Neda in Arcadian-Messenian myth.

replacement_candidates.name: Gulf of Kyparissia
replacement_candidates.relationship: Large Ionian Sea bay along the coast of Kyparissia (medieval Arcadia).
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: c. 20 CE (Strabo, Geography 8.3.22, as Kyparissian Gulf)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Named after ancient Kyparissia ('cypress-town').

replacement_candidates.name: Messenians
replacement_candidates.relationship: Ancient Greek people inhabiting Messenia, including the Pamisos plain and Kalamata (ancient Pharai).
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested in archaic Greek poetry (Tyrtaeus, 7th century BCE) and Herodotus (circa 700 BCE).
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Derived from the regional name Messene / Messenia.

replacement_candidates.name: Pamisos
replacement_candidates.relationship: Largest river of Messenia, emptying into the Messenian Gulf west of Kalamata.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Pre-Greek Messenian hydronym.

replacement_candidates.name: Messenian Gulf
replacement_candidates.relationship: Gulf of the Ionian Sea at whose northern head Kalamata lies.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: c. 20 CE (Strabo, Geography 8.4.1, as Messenian Gulf)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Named after the region of Messenia.

replacement_candidates.name: Leleges
replacement_candidates.relationship: Pre-Hellenic Aegean people associated with early Laconia and Messenia.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Aegean ethnonym of pre-Greek origin.

replacement_candidates.name: Sapientza
replacement_candidates.relationship: Island lying directly off the coast of Methoni (Modon).
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: c. 170 CE (Pausanias 4.34.12 as Oinoussai; Venetian Sapienza)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Oinoussai; medieval Venetian Sapienza ('wisdom').

replacement_candidates.name: Cape Matapan
replacement_candidates.relationship: Southernmost cape of the Peloponnese near the Messenian-Laconian littoral.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: c. 700 BCE (Homeric Hymn to Apollo 412, as Tainaron)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Tainaron; medieval Matapan possibly from Doric metopon ('forehead').

replacement_candidates.name: Mysians
replacement_candidates.relationship: Ancient inhabitants of Mysia in northwestern Anatolia.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Anatolian ethnonym attested in Homer and Herodotus.

replacement_candidates.name: Biga Çayı
replacement_candidates.relationship: Ancient Granicus River emptying into the Sea of Marmara near Karabiga (Pagaea).
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Granikos; Turkish Biga Çayı.

replacement_candidates.name: Sea of Marmara
replacement_candidates.relationship: Inland sea (ancient Propontis) on whose southern shore Pagaea sits.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: c. 470 BCE (Aeschylus and Herodotus, as Propontis)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Propontis ('before the Pontus/Black Sea'); Marmara from marble-rich Proconnesus.

replacement_candidates.name: Locrians
replacement_candidates.relationship: Ancient Greek tribe of Epicnemidian Locris where Mendenitsa (Boudounitsa) sits.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Greek Lokroi, attested since Homer.

replacement_candidates.name: Spercheios
replacement_candidates.relationship: Main river north of Mount Kallidromo and Thermopylae.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: From Greek sperkho ('to hasten/rush').

replacement_candidates.name: Kallidromo
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain ridge directly above Mendenitsa (Boudounitsa) and Thermopylae.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 191 BCE (Livy, Ab Urbe Condita 36.15, as Callidromus)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Greek Kallidromon ('fair-running' / 'good path').
